svg.text: b1 Bought press + OTP applicator in post-feed; a printer-axis shuttle presents one conductor at a time
Side elevation, looking along the carrier strip (schematic, not to scale)
Plan, looking down (schematic, not to scale)
fires on a relay; one fast stroke
ram finger: spring V on the ram (or the
applicator's wire hold spring); lifts with the ram
next contact waits one pitch upstream (into the page);
it slides in on the downstroke
the other split conductors: folded back 180 deg as ONE flat band
crimped ones return to their place, box in a pocket
valley-tine fork: pivot at the clamp edge, two 0.25 mm tines, holds Y only (slot open downward)
neck fork: proof pull 20 N after the stroke
ELP camera: the waiting contact upstream at rest,
the tip over the anvil, the finished crimp
shuttle: MGN12 rails, NEMA 17 + Tr8x2 (Prime rows)
Y (into the page): index to the next conductor
split 8-15 mm: tooling depth 6-12 mm [estimate] + bend and fork [calc geometry s1]
Reference for 'fixed': the applicator locates the contact; the ram finger's V, bolted to the ram,
puts the conductor on the crimp axis at first die touch; axial depth comes from the cassette datum.
Lateral capture in the open insulation wings: clone +/-0.21-0.83 mm, JST envelope +/-0.08-0.18 mm [TS s4].
contact pitch on strip ~7.1 mm [facts, Wurth analog]
the band lies back over the top plate, in ribbon order
A neighbour left flat in the anvil plane at 1.7 or 2.5 mm spacing sits inside the punch zone
[calc geometry s1]; with the strip attached the only open side is behind the tooling,
so every conductor except the target lies back in the band.
